evidence: Cic. Att. 1.16.11: cōnsuētūdine conjūnctī inter nōs sumus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: social intercourse, companionship, familiarity, in Cicero mostly in an honourable sense, and often with familiāritās. “Keep me company” is said with the person: manē mēcum.

terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.71: comes meus fuit, et omnium itinerum meōrum socius (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Manē, quaesō, mēcum; sōlus esse nōlō.
phrases.english: Keep me company, please; I don’t want to be alone.

sources: Lewis & Short: consuetudo · Lewis & Short: comes · Lewis & Short: colo
